Your motion-transfer prompt

✓ UNLOCKED
Use the uploaded reference video as the exact motion reference. Track the main subject’s full-body movement, posture, head movement, shoulder movement, hand/arm gestures, walking direction, weight shifts, and facial reactions frame-by-frame. Preserve the original body-motion timing and choreography as closely as possible. The generated subject should follow the same poses, transitions, head turns, body orientation, gestures, and natural pauses as the reference video. Keep human anatomy realistic and stable throughout the entire clip. Maintain consistent face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions, and identity. No unnatural limb movement, no extra fingers or limbs, no body warping, no sudden pose changes. Match the original camera movement, framing, perspective, shot transitions, and pacing. Keep the motion smooth, cinematic, realistic, and physically believable. Use subtle natural secondary motion in the hair and clothing while maintaining accurate body-motion tracking. IMPORTANT: Prioritize accurate motion transfer from the reference video over creating new choreography. Do not change the timing or direction of the subject’s movements.
